issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/NaN to 0, changing the prior toNumber NaN-propagation semantics.
issues.detail: The old panLinear used toNumber as lift, so non-numeric input produced NaN downstream. The new coerceNumber substitutes 0, silently altering observable output for malformed input. This is a behavior change hidden inside a typing PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new mapping in the release notes.

issues.description: Domain parameter typed as number[] but body requires NonEmptyArray; the type contract is under-specified.
issues.detail: pan/zoom read domain[0] and peek(domain) as distinct endpoints and now throw on empty input. The signature should be NonEmptyArray<number> (or readonly [number, ...number[]]) so the type system enforces the invariant the body asserts. Half-typed leaves the runtime check as the only backstop and leaks the abstraction.

issues.description: Empty-domain inputs now throw instead of soft-failing with NaN; strengthened precondition on a public API.
issues.detail: The prior implementation accepted any array and produced NaN via peek-of-empty arithmetic. The new code throws. This is an LSP-relevant contract change at the module boundary. Document it in release notes and the type signature, or restore non-throwing behavior for backwards compatibility.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before delegating, and only Linear empty-domain is tested.
issues.detail: panLog and zoomLog call Math.sign(domain[0]) before pan/zoom runs its isNonEmpty guard, so empty input produces sign=NaN before the error throws. The error still fires, but order is sloppy and Log/Pow/Symlog empty-domain paths are untested. Guard at entry points or extend test coverage.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the existing accessors.identity import without justification.
issues.detail: The previous file imported identity from './accessors.js'; the new file defines a local identity: TransformFn = x => x and drops the import. Functionally equivalent for numbers but diverges from codebase voice and duplicates an existing utility. Keep the import or add a comment justifying the narrower-typed local.

issues.description: peek overload pair is correct but needs a JSDoc comment explaining the non-empty precondition.
issues.detail: The overload returning T only fires when callers have already proven non-emptiness in the type system. Inside pan/zoom after isNonEmpty the parameter type is still number[], so peek returns number|undefined. A short JSDoc on the overload's intended use would help future readers and document the ADT refinement.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a scoped TypeScript port of transform.js with one quiet semantic shift and one under-specified type contract. coerceNumber silently swaps toNumber's null-returning behavior for a 0-coercion, changing observable output on malformed input — all three reviewers flagged this as the headline issue. The Domain parameter is typed as number[] while the body requires non-empty input, leaving the runtime guard as the only backstop. Smaller items: empty-domain now throws (contract change), Log variants probe domain[0] before the guard, local identity shadows an existing import, and the peek overload pair needs a JSDoc. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on coerceNumber semantics and Domain typing before landing.
